# jsontext — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 4 · S2 E3 A4 H3 P3 · limited by audit (none recorded) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — Go 1.26 `encoding/json`, Rust `serde_json`, CPython `json` string encoding (surveyed 2026-11-08, from their documented behaviour, not by reading their source)

**Audit:** review none · mutation none · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz none · ct n/a — no secret: the module only formats caller-supplied text

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

## Compared with

Surveyed 2026-11-08 per `SURVEY-PLAYBOOK.md`; from documented behaviour *(inferred)*, no source was read or run. Stars and activity not recorded.

| Project | Language | Licence | Stars | Last release / push | What a user notices against this module |
|---|---|---|--:|---|---|
| [Go `encoding/json`](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/json) — **reference** | Go | BSD-3-Clause | — | Go 1.26 | String encoder escapes `"` `\` controls, `<` `>` `&` and U+2028/2029 by default (`SetEscapeHTML(false)` turns that off); ill-formed UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD **per byte**; never `\uXXXX` for printable non-ASCII. No ASCII-only mode. |
| [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json) | Rust | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | — | — | Escapes `"` `\` and controls; non-ASCII verbatim; input is `&str`, so ill-formed UTF-8 cannot occur. No HTML or ASCII-only option. |
| [CPython `json`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html) | Python | PSF-2.0 | — | 3.14 | `ensure_ascii=True` (default) writes every non-ASCII scalar as `\uXXXX` with surrogate pairs and also escapes DEL; `False` leaves them. Lone surrogates in a `str` are written as-is. No HTML option. |

**Where we are ahead:** an explicit policy for bytes that are not UTF-8 (`replace` per maximal subpart / `escape_bytes` / `reject`), the escape switches of all three libraries (HTML, ASCII-only, plain) in one writer, and a nesting prescan the three do not offer · **Where we are behind:** no streaming `Encoder` object and no `std.json.Stringify` integration (use `std.json.Stringify` for values; this module is for a string that arrives as bytes); no `\uXXXX` for DEL under `ascii_only` (CPython does; Go does not, and DEL is not a JSON control character — see below).

## What this module is, and what it is not

Two pieces of JSON *text* handling that a dozen modules each wrote again: `writeString` / `writeStringContents` (a JSON string literal from arbitrary bytes) and `depthWithin` (bracket depth of a buffer, string-aware, before a parser allocates). It parses nothing, builds no documents, validates no JSON, and does not write numbers, keys or separators (`std.json.Stringify` does). The caller picks the options at compile time (`StringOptions` is a `comptime` parameter), so the default loop that `accesslog` benchmarked is the one `.{}` compiles to.

Not here, by decision:

- **Number formatting, key ordering, pretty printing, object writers.** `std.json.Stringify` owns them. *Never* in this module: it would make it a second JSON library.
- **Escaping DEL (0x7F).** RFC 8259 §7 does not list it; Go and serde_json do not escape it. CPython's `ensure_ascii` does. Not now; if a consumer needs it, add `StringOptions.escape_del`.
- **Lone surrogates.** A Zig `[]const u8` is UTF-8, where a surrogate (`ED A0..BF`) is ill-formed and goes through the `invalid_utf8` policy. There is no WTF-8 mode. Never (no caller has WTF-8).
- **A per-byte U+FFFD policy (Go's).** Refused: the maximal-subpart policy is the Unicode / WHATWG recommendation. The two differ only on a truncated valid prefix; the tests pin the difference.
- **Escaping `/`.** Never written as `\/`; only needed inside `</script>`, which `html_safe` already covers by escaping `<`.

## Performance

Not measured here: the module has no bench of its own. The string writer is the code `accesslog` benchmarked (`modules/accesslog/src/bench.zig`, opt-in `ACCESSLOG_BENCH=1`, against a frozen byte-at-a-time baseline), whose `writeJsonLines` now calls it: the ASCII hot-path row was 271.4 ns before the move and 273.9 ns after (ReleaseFast, 2026-11-08, best of 5 rounds), valid UTF-8 362.5 to 343.8, ill-formed 477.4 to 401.7 — noise-level, no regression. No comparison against Go or Rust encoders was made.

## Wire format / algorithm

RFC 8259 §7. The string literal is `"` + contents + `"`. Contents: `"` → `\"`, `\` → `\\`, `0x08 0x09 0x0A 0x0C 0x0D` → `\b \t \n \f \r`, every other byte below 0x20 → `\u00xx` (lowercase hex), everything else verbatim unless an option applies. UTF-8 classification follows Unicode 16.0 Table 3-7 and the maximal-subpart rule of §3.9 (`utf8Step`). `ascii_only` writes a scalar above U+FFFF as the UTF-16 surrogate pair `\ud83d\ude00` (lowercase hex); `html_safe` adds `<`, `>`, `&` (`\u003c`, `\u003e`, `\u0026`) and U+2028 / U+2029.

The scan is table-driven: one lookup per byte for the verbatim set; well-formed runs are flushed with one `writeAll` when an escape interrupts. Nothing is allocated.

`depthWithin(bytes, max)` is one pass tracking `in_string` / `escaped`; `[`/`{` outside a string increase depth, `]`/`}` decrease it (saturating at 0). It does not validate — the doc comment lists exactly what it accepts.

## Limits and refusals

- `depthWithin` cap is the caller's `max_depth` (a `usize`); the scan is O(n) and uses constant space, so it can be run on a hostile buffer before a parser.
- `.reject` returns `error.InvalidUtf8` after writing the opening quote and the complete output before the bad byte's run; the writer is then left with a partial literal. A caller that cannot tolerate that checks first with `std.unicode.utf8ValidateSlice`.
- No consumer-reachable panic: every public function is total on any bytes; the only `unreachable` is in `accesslog`'s wrapper, on an error the chosen options cannot return.

## Anchoring

- **Default options**: the byte-exact policy is pinned by the tests here (literal expected strings written from the Unicode text, a std-validator sweep and a brute-force maximal-subpart check for the classifier) and, through `accesslog`, by its frozen foreign oracle (`modules/accesslog/tools/json_oracle.py` run against CPython `json`, Go `encoding/json` and jq 1.8.1, replayed by `modules/accesslog/src/json_oracle_test.zig`).
- **`ascii_only`**: the non-trivial expected values in the test (`€`, `😀`, `é`) were read off CPython `json.dumps(…, ensure_ascii=True)` on 2026-11-08 and written down; there is no live oracle in `tools/`. Re-derived rather than a standing external anchor.
- **`html_safe`**: the escape set is Go's documented `HTMLEscape` set, expected values written by hand (self).
- Every option combination is round-tripped through `std.json` (a parser that is not this module's) in a test.

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle MIXED

## Open

- A standing oracle for `ascii_only` / `html_safe` in `tools/` (CPython and Go) like accesslog's, to lift the evidence grade; also a fuzz harness (`fuzz none`).
- Move the remaining string-escaper copies onto this module (health, openapi, jinja, cbor diag, mcp, jsonshape, framing's `jsonDepthWithin`); until then each keeps its copy. Health's differs: DEL escaped, and a whole string with any ill-formed byte has every byte >= 0x80 escaped (including valid sequences) — `escape_bytes` here escapes only the ill-formed bytes, a deliberate narrowing the health move must accept.
